nodes.line: Keep your voice down. The rain doesn't cover as much as it used to. Neither do the trees.

options.label: Ask for work
options.response: There's a courier run. No package, no paperwork, no questions. Standard arrangement.

options.label: Ask about a routing cover sheet
options.response: A cover sheet. In this economy. Lucky for you, the rain keeps old paperwork legible around here. Don't ask where it dried.

options.label: Mention the Form 27-B you are definitely not filling in
options.response: Paper gets wet up here. Wet paper gets lost. Consider yours lost in exactly the right direction.

options.label: Report in after orientation
options.response: I heard. The ridge heard. The cameras that work heard. You're on the roster. Bring rain gear.

options.label: Ask where the scrap goes
options.response: Up the logging roads, mostly. Cameras up here are half unplugged. The other half are watching the wrong ridge.

options.label: Move along
options.response: Smart. Standing still is how you get catalogued.

options.label: Ask about the informant census
options.response: There's a headcount. There is no headcount. Sign in and visit every one of us — twelve of us, coast to coast — and the circuit owes you a badge. A plastic one. It's official.

options.label: Present your census card for a countersign
options.response: "Moss" presses a damp thumb to the card. "Paper rots up here. This one we keep dry. You are counted."

options.label: Have Moss mark the real crossings
options.response: Moss circles three. 'These are ferries. The rest are weather with a schedule. Don't ride the weather.'

nodes.line: You carry nothing, you know nothing, you were never here. Deliver nothing to no one. Clear?

options.label: Nod slowly
options.response: Good. The less you understand, the safer we both are.

options.label: Ask what's actually in the package
options.response: There is no package. There was never a package. You're learning.

nodes.line: Half the cameras on this ridge aren't wired to anything. The other half are wired wrong. I keep the map.

options.label: Ask about the map
options.response: The map is in my head. The head stays on my shoulders. That's the arrangement.

options.label: Ask about the terminal
options.response: Timber terminal, mostly. Flock thinks we ship something else. We ship timber. It's almost disappointing.

options.label: Leave her to it
options.response: Watch the ridge line. The unplugged ones are the ones that matter.

options.label: Report the verified count
options.response: Priya logs it. 'Counters counting counters. At least now we know which ones to trust. Good work.'

options.label: Ask about the trailhead sensors
options.response: The trail counters count hikers, but somebody's been counting the counters. Get me the numbers from the ridge and have the clerk at the visitor center confirm the firmware is stock.

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Harbor Engineer Priya signs with a muddy thumb. 'Counted. The hatch keys talk to each other, you know. Now they'll know you.'

nodes.line: Welcome to Seattle! Can I interest you in a latte, and also your hiking itinerary?

options.label: Order the latte
options.response: Oat milk? And while I steam this — any plans to visit the old logging roads? Purely for the trail recommendations.

options.label: Ask about Form 27-B
options.response: We don't... stock that form. Officially. I can stamp a requisition that says you never asked. The requisition is the form. Welcome to the Bureau.

options.label: Present Boomer Dave's Form 12-F
options.response: Form 12-F, lawn ownership, out of state. I can stamp it, but it needs a routing cover sheet first. The cover sheet office was abolished. You'll want someone... unofficial.

options.label: Ask for an official stamp
options.response: Timesheets from Atlanta? Stamping things is my whole personality. Stamped. Twice. The second stamp makes it more official. That's just math.

options.label: Submit the form for review
options.response: Reviewed. Notarized. Denied appeal filed on your behalf. Outstanding requirement: Garrett Langley's own signature. The founder is in Atlanta. Enjoy the commute.

options.label: Present the signed Form 27-B
options.response: Signed? By an actual agent? I need to... yes. The stamp. You've earned it. The Bureau recognizes you. Paperwork fears you now.

options.label: Decline to share your itinerary
options.response: Of course! Privacy! I respect that. I'll just note down 'unaccompanied, evasive' for the welcome survey.

options.label: Leave the visitor center
options.response: Come back anytime! The cameras out front are just for weather. Weather and tourism.

options.label: Ask Cole to verify the counter firmware
options.response: Cole plugs it in between lattes. 'Stock firmware. The extras are purely decorative. Like the steamed milk of surveillance.'

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Barista-Inspector Cole stamps your card without looking up. 'Filed. Countersigned. Never happened. Next window.'

name: Mara Chen
role: Ferry Signal Technician, Municipal Visitor Center

nodes.line: The ferries use foghorns. The new signals use passenger names.

options.label: Ask about the ferry logs
options.response: Ferries log passengers who never board and cargo that never lands. I need the manifest cross-checked by someone the rain doesn't bother. Moss knows which crossings are real.

options.label: Ask about the ferry signals
options.response: Every crossing reports its passengers twice: once to shore and once somewhere inland.

options.label: Ask what moves in the fog
options.response: Boats, mostly. The antennas move only when nobody is looking.

options.label: Return the maintenance badge
options.response: Keep it dry. The scanner trusts water damage more than people.

options.label: Present your circuit card for a countersign
options.response: Mara Chen countersigns your card. 'Counted on the circuit. Keep moving.'
